The hooks run noskills as "npx eser@latest noskills", and npx can wait on the network before noskills starts. Claude Code, Codex, Copilot CLI and Kiro let a tool call go ahead when its PreToolUse hook does not answer within 30 seconds, so the git guard and the protected-file check would not apply to that call. Install the eser CLI (npm install -g eser, or deno install -g -A jsr:@eserstack/cli) and run "eser noskills init" so the hooks call the installed command.

#!/bin/sh
# Generated by noskills when an agent session starts; edits are overwritten.
#
# Agent sessions find this file first on PATH, so every git process they start
# runs through it. Reads, clones and commands on other repositories run
# directly. Everything else is checked by noskills, which refuses git writes to
# the project's repository, and pushes from anywhere, while allowGit is false.

real_git='/usr/bin/git'
project_git_dir='/p/.git'

# Find the subcommand and its first argument after git's own options.
subcommand=''
first_arg=''
found=0
takes_value=0
for arg in "$@"; do
  if [ "$found" = 1 ]; then
    first_arg=$arg
    break
  fi
  if [ "$takes_value" = 1 ]; then
    takes_value=0
    continue
  fi
  case $arg in
    -C|-c|--git-dir|--work-tree|--namespace|--super-prefix|--config-env|--attr-source) takes_value=1 ;;
    -C?*|-c?*|--git-dir=*|--work-tree=*|--namespace=*|--super-prefix=*|--config-env=*|--attr-source=*|--exec-path=*) ;;
    --no-replace-objects|--no-lazy-fetch|--no-advice|--bare|--no-optional-locks|--literal-pathspecs|--glob-pathspecs|--noglob-pathspecs|--icase-pathspecs|--no-pager|-P|--paginate|-p) ;;
    *)
      subcommand=$arg
      found=1
      ;;
  esac
done

case $subcommand in
  ''|log|diff|status|show|blame|rev-parse|ls-files|ls-tree|cat-file|describe|shortlog|name-rev|for-each-ref|rev-list|help|version|--version|-v|--help|-h|--exec-path|--html-path|--man-path|--info-path|clone) exec "$real_git" "$@" ;;
  branch)
    case $first_arg in
      ''|--list|-l|-a|--all|-r|--remotes|-v|--verbose|--contains|--no-contains|--merged|--no-merged|--show-current) exec "$real_git" "$@" ;;
    esac
    ;;
  tag)
    case $first_arg in
      ''|-l|--list|-v|--verify|-n) exec "$real_git" "$@" ;;
    esac
    ;;
  stash)
    case $first_arg in
      list|show) exec "$real_git" "$@" ;;
    esac
    ;;
  remote)
    case $first_arg in
      ''|-v|--verbose|show|get-url) exec "$real_git" "$@" ;;
    esac
    ;;
  reflog)
    case $first_arg in
      ''|show) exec "$real_git" "$@" ;;
    esac
    ;;
esac

# A write with no option before the subcommand acts on the repository that the
# working directory (or GIT_DIR) selects. Outside the project it runs directly.
# An option this script does not know stands where the subcommand would be;
# the options after it may name any repository, so noskills decides.
case $subcommand in
  push|send-pack|-*) ;;
  *)
    if [ "$1" = "$subcommand" ]; then
      target_git_dir=$("$real_git" rev-parse --path-format=absolute --git-common-dir 2>/dev/null) || target_git_dir=''
      if [ "$target_git_dir" != "$project_git_dir" ]; then
        exec "$real_git" "$@"
      fi
    fi
    ;;
esac

# The command may change directory before noskills starts (deno task does), so
# the working directory git would run in travels as NOSKILLS_GIT_CWD.
git_cwd=$(pwd -P)

# The check may never answer (npx can wait on the registry), so a watcher stops
# it after 30 seconds: SIGTERM, then SIGKILL 2 seconds later.
# The check writes to a file rather than to this script's stderr, so a process
# it leaves behind cannot keep the caller's pipe open.
check_log=$(mktemp "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/noskills-git-check.XXXXXX") || {
  printf '%s\n' "noskills: could not create a temporary file to check \"git $subcommand\", so it did not run." >&2
  exit 1
}
NOSKILLS_REAL_GIT=$real_git NOSKILLS_GIT_CWD=$git_cwd NOSKILLS_PROJECT_ROOT='/p'\''s dir' npx eser@latest noskills invoke-hook git-exec "$@" </dev/null >"$check_log" 2>&1 &
check_pid=$!
(
  watch_status=0
  trap 'kill "$nap_pid" 2>/dev/null; exit "$watch_status"' TERM
  sleep 30 &
  nap_pid=$!
  wait "$nap_pid"
  watch_status=124
  kill -TERM "$check_pid" 2>/dev/null
  sleep 2 &
  nap_pid=$!
  wait "$nap_pid"
  kill -KILL "$check_pid" 2>/dev/null
  exit 124
) </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 &
watch_pid=$!
trap 'kill "$check_pid" "$watch_pid" 2>/dev/null; rm -f "$check_log"; exit 1' HUP INT TERM
# The shell's notice for a stopped job would reach the agent; the message below
# says what happened instead.
wait "$check_pid" 2>/dev/null
status=$?
kill "$watch_pid" 2>/dev/null
wait "$watch_pid" 2>/dev/null
watch_status=$?
trap - HUP INT TERM
cat "$check_log" >&2
rm -f "$check_log"

if [ "$status" -ne 0 ]; then
  if [ "$watch_status" -eq 124 ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "noskills: the check for \"git $subcommand\" did not answer within 30 seconds, so it did not run. When command in .eser/manifest.yml starts noskills through npx, install noskills and set command to the installed one, so the check does not wait on the network." >&2
  elif [ "$status" -ne 3 ]; then
    printf '%s\n' "noskills: could not check \"git $subcommand\" (exit status $status), so it did not run." >&2
  fi
  exit 1
fi
exec "$real_git" "$@"
